2:
\textbf{(a)} $\ln(2+5x)=\ln2+\ln\big(1+\tfrac{5x}{2}\big)$ and $\ln(1+u)=\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{(-1)^{n+1}u^n}{n}$:
\[\boxed{\ln(2+5x)=\ln2+\sum_{n=1}^\infty\frac{(-1)^{n+1}5^n}{n\,2^n}x^n}=\ln2+\tfrac52x-\tfrac{25}{8}x^2+\cdots\]
\textbf{(b)} Ratio test: $\Big|\frac{a_{n+1}}{a_n}\Big|=\frac{n}{n+1}\cdot\frac{5|x|}{2}\to\frac{5|x|}{2}$, so it converges for $|x|<\frac25$. At $x=\frac25$ it is the alternating harmonic series (converges); at $x=-\frac25$ it is $-\sum\frac1n$ (diverges). So it converges on \boxed{\big(-\tfrac25,\ \tfrac25\big]} (any interval inside this, such as $(-0.4,0.4)$, is also acceptable).
3:
$AD$ and $BC$ join opposite corners of the cube, so they are main (body) diagonals. Put the cube at $[0,1]^3$; two body diagonals are $\langle1,1,1\rangle$ and $\langle1,1,-1\rangle$ (up to sign):
\[\cos\theta=\frac{|1+1-1|}{\sqrt3\sqrt3}=\frac13\ \Rightarrow\ \theta=\cos^{-1}\tfrac13\approx\boxed{70.5^\circ}.\]
4:
Line 1: point $(0,-1,5)$, direction $\langle4,2,-4\rangle$. Line 2: set $x-1=1-y=\frac z3=s$: point $(1,1,0)$, direction $\langle1,-1,3\rangle$. Normal:
\[\langle4,2,-4\rangle\times\langle1,-1,3\rangle=\langle2,-16,-6\rangle\parallel\langle1,-8,-3\rangle.\]
Through $(0,-1,5)$: $x-8(y+1)-3(z-5)=0$:
\[\boxed{x-8y-3z+7=0}\quad(\text{check }(1,1,0):\ 1-8+7=0).\]
5:
For $y=x^4$: $y'=4x^3$, $y''=12x^2$, so
\[\kappa(x)=\frac{12x^2}{(1+16x^6)^{3/2}}.\]
By the quotient rule, the numerator of $\kappa'(x)$ is $24x(1+16x^6)^{3/2}-12x^2\cdot\frac32(1+16x^6)^{1/2}\cdot96x^5$. Dividing by $(1+16x^6)^{1/2}$, $\kappa'=0$ when
\[24x(1+16x^6)-1728x^7=0\ \Rightarrow\ 24x=1344x^7\ \Rightarrow\ x^6=\frac1{56}\ (x\ne0).\]
$\kappa(0)=0$ and $\kappa\to0$ as $|x|\to\infty$, so these give the maximum:
\[\boxed{\Big(\pm56^{-1/6},\ 56^{-2/3}\Big)}\approx(\pm0.511,\ 0.068).\]
6:
\textbf{(a)} $\vec r\,'(t)=\langle\pi\cos\pi t,\,-\pi\sin\pi t,\,2t-1\rangle$, so $\vec r\,'(2)=\langle\pi,0,3\rangle$ and $\vec r(2)=\langle0,1,2\rangle$. Normal plane:
\[\pi(x-0)+0(y-1)+3(z-2)=0\ \Rightarrow\ \boxed{\pi x+3z=6}.\]
\textbf{(b)} $z=t^2-t=0$ at $t=0$ and $t=1$:
\[L=\int_0^1\sqrt{\pi^2\cos^2\pi t+\pi^2\sin^2\pi t+(2t-1)^2}\,dt=\int_0^1\sqrt{\pi^2+(2t-1)^2}\,dt.\]
7:
$\vec v=\langle2t,\,-t^{-2},\,1\rangle$, $\vec a=\langle2,\,2t^{-3},\,0\rangle$.

\textbf{(a)} $\vec v\cdot\vec a=4t-2t^{-5}=0\Rightarrow t^6=\frac12\Rightarrow t=\boxed{2^{-1/6}\approx0.891}$.

\textbf{(b)} There $\vec a\perp\vec v$, so $a_T=\frac{\vec v\cdot\vec a}{|\vec v|}=\boxed{0}$ and $a_N=|\vec a|=\sqrt{4+4t^{-6}}=\sqrt{4+8}=\boxed{2\sqrt3}$.
8:
$x=r\cos\theta$, so $dx=\cos\theta\,dr-r\sin\theta\,d\theta$. At $r=2$, $\theta=\frac\pi6$: $x=\sqrt3$ and
\[|dx|\le\frac{\sqrt3}{2}(0.05)+2\cdot\frac12(0.1)\approx0.0433+0.1=0.1433.\]
So $x\approx\sqrt3\pm0.143$, i.e. roughly \boxed{1.589\le x\le1.875}.
9:
Minimize $M=x^2+y^2+z^2$ subject to $g=xy^2z^4=1$ (so $x,y,z>0$). Lagrange: $\nabla M=\lambda\nabla g$:
\[2x=\lambda y^2z^4,\quad 2y=2\lambda xyz^4,\quad 2z=4\lambda xy^2z^3.\]
Multiply each by $x$, $y$, $z$ and use $xy^2z^4=1$: $2x^2=\lambda$, $2y^2=2\lambda$, $2z^2=4\lambda$, so $x^2=\frac\lambda2$, $y^2=\lambda$, $z^2=2\lambda$. Then $x^2y^4z^8=\frac\lambda2\cdot\lambda^2\cdot16\lambda^4=8\lambda^7=1$, so $\lambda=2^{-3/7}$:
\[\boxed{x=\sqrt{\lambda/2}\approx0.610,\quad y=\sqrt\lambda\approx0.862,\quad z=\sqrt{2\lambda}\approx1.219}\]
with minimum $M=\frac72\lambda\approx2.600$.
10:
\textbf{(a)} The solid lies over the half-disk where $z=x\ge0$, under $z=x$. In polar coordinates:
\[V=\int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2}\int_0^2(r\cos\theta)\,r\,dr\,d\theta\qquad\Big(\text{or }\int_0^2\int_{-\sqrt{4-x^2}}^{\sqrt{4-x^2}}x\,dy\,dx\Big).\]
\textbf{(b)} Reverse the order: the region is $0\le y\le x\le\frac\pi2$:
\[\int_0^{\pi/2}\int_0^x\frac{\sin x}{x}\,dy\,dx=\int_0^{\pi/2}\sin x\,dx=\boxed{1}.\]
